chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, who raised it, said:
Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: There is no problem with salat (prayer) in pure khazz. But as for that in which rabbit fur or other similar things are mixed, then do not perform salat (prayer) in it.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.الْخَالِصِ: pure, meaning unmixed with problematic material
key_terms.الْخَزِّ: khazz, a type of fabric mentioned as permissible when pure
key_terms.فَلَا تُصَلِّ: do not perform salat (prayer), indicating prohibition
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem, indicating permissibility
key_terms.وَبَرُ الْأَرْنَبِ: rabbit fur, cited here as a substance that invalidates praying in such a garment

ai.seo_question: Is salat (prayer) valid in clothing made of pure khazz or mixed with rabbit fur?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning garments worn in salat (prayer). It permits salat (prayer) in pure khazz, while prohibiting salat (prayer) in material mixed with rabbit fur or similar substances.
